channel.title: Zone1 Kitchen — sourced air-fryer articles
channel.description: Documentation-based air-fryer buying guides. Every factual sentence cites the manufacturer page or owner's manual it came from; no hands-on testing is claimed and no Amazon price or rating is published.

item.title: Dual-basket or countertop oven? The 8-quart question nobody answers
item.description: Two 3-quart drawers and one 26-quart cavity solve opposite problems. Here is the documented difference, and the one measurement that decides it for your kitchen.

item.title: What "450 °F" actually means on an air fryer listing
item.description: On one Chefman model it is a two-minute finishing blast. On another it is a setting the manual never mentions. The badge is the same. The feature is not.

item.title: 25 presets, 24 presets, or 10-in-1? One brand page says all three
item.description: A single official product page contradicts itself four ways. That is not a scandal; it is what an unmaintained product page looks like. Here is how to read it.

item.title: Why this affiliate site shows no Amazon prices, ratings or review counts
item.description: It is not an oversight and it is not humility. Amazon's Program Policies only permit those numbers under two specific conditions, and this site meets neither.

item.title: Two 3-quart drawers or one 8-quart basket: which actually feeds four people?
item.description: The total volume is nearly identical. The cooking is not, and the difference is what you do when the first batch finishes.

item.title: Chefman 6 Qt Dual Basket: a review of the documents, not the machine
item.description: No unit was bought, unboxed or cooked in. What follows is a reading of Chefman's own page and manual for the TurboFry Touch 6 Qt triple-verified SKU — what it promises, what it does not, and the one number the manufacturer withholds.

item.title: How to read an air fryer spec sheet: the eight lines that actually decide it
item.description: Listings are long on adjectives and short on the eight lines that determine whether a machine fits your kitchen. Walk them in this order and most of the market falls away before you look at a price.

item.title: 26 quarts, 1,519 cubic inches: an honest air fryer capacity guide
item.description: Quart capacity is a cavity measurement, not a food measurement. So this guide uses the numbers the manufacturers print, shows the arithmetic they imply, and is explicit about the one thing none of them publishes: usable food volume.

item.title: Will it actually fit? Three air fryers, measured against your counter
item.description: Every manufacturer on this site publishes outer dimensions. That turns 'will it fit' from a guess into arithmetic — and it is the one buying question a spec sheet can answer completely.

item.title: Who pays for the air-fryer review you are reading?
item.description: Affiliate links are not a scandal and they are not invisible. Here is exactly how this site earns, what Amazon requires it to say, and the three claims it is not allowed to make.

item.title: The 1,700-watt question: what an air fryer actually asks of your kitchen
item.description: All three units are documented at 1,700 watts on 120 volts. That number decides more than browning — it decides whether the appliance can share a circuit.

item.title: The 8-quart Chefman is sold as two different machines — and the listing describes both
item.description: One SKU tops out at 400°F. Another reaches 450°F for the final two minutes. The supplied Amazon link's title names the feature of one and the finish of the other.

item.title: Sync Finish, explained by the manual that ships with it
item.description: One button promises two baskets that end at the same time. The owner's manual spells out exactly how that works, exactly when it breaks, and what the other sync button does instead.

item.title: The aerosol-oil caution nobody reads, quoted instead of paraphrased
item.description: Chefman's dual-window manual carries one CAUTION about spray cans that decides whether a nonstick basket keeps its coating. The sentence is short enough to quote whole, so this page does.

item.title: 1700 watts, three manuals, and one extension-cord rule that is not the same
item.description: All three appliances in this set carry the same wattage rating from their manufacturers. Their manuals do not agree on how to power them, and one of the three rules is absolute.

item.title: Seven accessories, a six-accessory title, and one honest caveat
item.description: Two of Emeril's own documents say 7 accessories. Amazon's title for the same listing says six. The owner's manual settles the count and then takes it back — here is what each document actually says.

item.title: Rotisserie at home: what the 26 QT's manual actually documents
item.description: The preset and the spit set are in the manual. What the manual never claims — cooked weights, times, doneness — is the part worth reading before you plan a chicken dinner.

item.title: What 'As an Amazon Associate I earn from qualifying purchases' actually obliges
item.description: The sentence in this site's header is a contract clause with a mandated wording and a placement rule. Who requires it, what it must look like, and the things it does not do.

item.title: Air fryer gift guide 2026: match the format to the person
item.description: Two small baskets, one large basket, or a French-door countertop oven — the three formats in this guide are documented by their manufacturers, not tested by anyone here. Pick the format first; the model questions can wait until the box is open.

item.title: The Black Friday model-number switch, and the three-minute check that catches it
item.description: Discount badges stack up in November. The listings underneath them do not always describe the same machine - including the three this site tracks. Here is the documented version, and the check to run before the deal timer wins.

item.title: How to clean an air fryer, according to the people who made it
item.description: Three manuals in this set carry cleaning sections. Quoted side by side, they agree on the big rules and split on the details. No vinegar hacks and no life tricks - just the instructions in the box.

item.title: Chefman vs. Emeril: what a basket brand and an oven brand actually publish
item.description: Two brands, three machines, one decision. Both brand pages state capacity, footprint and temperature; neither states how dinner turns out. This is the comparison of what is written down, including the parts where the writing contradicts itself.

item.title: “98% less oil” is a sentence on a box, not a measurement
item.description: Chefman's 8 Qt page carries the phrase in its first line. Less than what, on which food, measured how, and by whom? The page does not say. Here is exactly what it does say, and four questions that work on any percentage printed on an appliance.

item.title: Eight questions to ask before you buy a multi-function kitchen appliance
item.description: A multi-function machine is a stack of claims: quarts, presets, temperature ranges, accessory counts. Every question below is answerable from a listing page, a spec block or the manual in the box — and each one has a live example in this site's own three-product record, including the places where the documents refuse to answer.
